Norm saturation forces equalities in Z*Z, yielding <U_i x,U_j y>=-<x,y>, precisely orthogonality of graph subspaces in C^q direct_sum C^p. Conversely that mixed identity makes the prescribed map on sum of initial supports isometric, extendable by zero, giving a common dual certificate. Bessel projection of the mutually orthonormal scaled graph basis to both coordinate blocks proves rank sum <=2p and <=2q. Signed E_jj and -E_jj saturate; m=2d implies rank one and orthonormal 2d graph basis. The off-diagonal unitary block equation yields sum A_i=0. New independent NumPy computed 161 exact-formula pairwise trace norm comparisons through d=6 and rectangular witnesses; floating-point checks supplement full algebraic proof.

value.rationale: Maximal triangle-equality separation is the natural diameter packing problem for noncommutative trace-class unit spheres. The sharp rectangular rank budget and complete saturated square geometry answer a precise extremal classification, and imply the optimal isometric matrix size for every finite star metric.

final_claim: For pairwise maximally trace-norm-separated nonzero complex p-by-q matrices, sum of matrix ranks <=2min(p,q), attained by signed diagonal units; exact pairwise condition is orthogonality of polar support graphs. For d-by-d saturated normalized rank-one families, the polar graph vectors form a balanced orthonormal basis, so their matrix sum is zero. The unit-edge star with m leaves embeds isometrically in M_d(C), trace norm, exactly when m<=2d.
